title: Add Core UNIX domain socket support
body:
This adds support for `unix://` as a protocol option. It's initial use is intended to reduce latency for the Godot debugger, especially with embedded support, which sends a lot of messages on macOS. Future iterations of other platforms may also switch to a similar approach.

| protocol | average latency |
| :---- | :---- |
| TCP | 16 µs |
| UNIX | 4 µs |

Later versions of Windows support `AF_UNIX`, so it could be added as an option too.

## Usage

Launching the Godot editor with `--debug-server=unix:///tmp/godot.sock` will use UDS instead of TCP.

## API Improvements

### UNIX domain socket support

Godot introduces two new classes to interact with UNIX domain sockets:

- `UDSServer`: a complement to `TCPServer`, for creating servers that listed on a UNIX domain socket.
- `StreamPeerUDS`: a complement to `StreamPeerTCP`, which is a specialised `StreamPeer` for UNIX domain sockets.

### Writing code that is agnostic of the transport (TCP or UNIX domain socket)

Both TCP and UNIX domain sockets are connect-based APIs, build on the same underlying OS APIs, so once a connection has been established, user code can be agnostic of the transport. The `StreamPeerSocket` has APIs for checking the status or disconnecting from the host.

Users can write code agnostic code in GDScript, C# or via GDExtensions by using the parent classes:

- `SocketServer`
- `StreamPeerSocket`

### Agnostic server code

You might have code to start a TCP or UNIX socket server like:

```gdscript
func start_uds() -> SocketServer:
	var server := UDSServer.new()
	server.listen("/tmp/test.sock")
	return server
	
func start_tcp() -> SocketServer:
	var server := TCPServer.new()
	server.listen(8889)
	return server
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Both functions return a `SocketServer`, which contains the common behaviour for both TCP and UNIX domain socket servers

The `SocketServer` instance can be passed to a function than can accept connections using the `take_socket_connection` API, which returns a `StreamPeerSocket`:

```gdscript
func run_server(server: SocketServer) -> void:
	var cn: StreamPeerSocket = server.take_socket_connection()
	handle_conn(cn)
```

Your `handle_conn` function will accept a `StreamPeerSocket` instance, which is a common base class for TCP and UNIX peers:

```gdscript
func handle_conn(cn: StreamPeerSocket) -> void:
	# Some loop to handle the connection
	
	if cn.get_status() == StreamPeerSocket.STATUS_ERROR:
		cn.disconnect_from_host()
```

### Agnostic client code

The client side will be similar, with only the connection method differing:

```gdscript
func connect_tcp() -> StreamPeerSocket:
	var cn := StreamPeerTCP.new()
	cn.connect_to_host("127.0.0.1", 8889)
	return cn
	
func connect_uds() -> StreamPeerSocket:
	var cn := StreamPeerUDS.new()
	cn.connect_to_host("/tmp/test.sock")
	return cn
```

In both cases, we return the `StreamPeerSocket`, which allows the code to be agnostic of the transport (TCP or UNIX domain socket).

## Compatibility

✅ Verified GDExtension compatibility by calling `get_status` on `StreamPeerTCP`. The following code was compiled against the 4.4.1 extension API and then executed against this branch successfully.

```cpp
Ref<StreamPeerTCP> client;
client.instantiate();
StreamPeerTCP::Status s = client->get_status();
```

## Testing

Added unit tests for UDS, similar to the TCP tests.

## Future

Future plan is to select `unix://` automatically when running / debugging an embedded process.
